items.title: Ed Polcer interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998
items.q: Also my ex-partner, Red Balaban, who I’d been working with when I quit my day job, he put me on a partial salary to go out and book his band... ctx.x: It was a good answer. When it came down to making a living when you were a young man, you were going to take a crack at being a full time musician.

Oh yeah. This came after I worked for a couple of years in engineering and purchasing, yeah. That was my midlife crisis see. A lot of very fortunate things happened to me at that time. I guess I was in my late 30s and my first marriage, which was very good for several years, sort of petered out as I got more and more involved in music and less and less involved with a business career and the success thing which I think my ex-wife expected me to do. In all fairness to her she married a Princeton grad and probably…

player. And so since then I’ve had this strength behind me to get into music. You know what I’m saying. This massive move to give up my day job and get into music wasn’t done alone, it was done with a lot of help. Also my ex-partner, Red Balaban, who I’d been working with when I quit my day job, he put me on a partial salary to go out and book his band, Balaban and Cats.
